title: Best early trombonists and moving back to New Orleans in 1926
summary: Question of best trombonists; Nelson moved back about 1926, and was the only trombonist in the country area.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: When you were young, who were the best trombonists around town in the early days that you can remember? Hearing music? When did you move here? You didn't hear music much before you left town, I guess, here to go up to… How old were you when you went to Napoleonville? Oh, I was a baby.
Yeah. When did you move back here? Oh, let's see.

Moved back here, I imagine, about 1926. My daughter was born in 27, she was born here. My son was born in 25, he was born in the country. Now you ask me who was the best trombone player? No, that's pretty nice.
Or even up in the country, wherever you heard music.

I was the only trombone player out in that part. And they had a fellow, like I was telling you, Professor Claiborne Williams' brother, and they had another fellow there, the James boys, well he wasn't so much on trombone, he got off a bass to trombone, his instrument was bass. You understand?
